title: hwp-edit-report-v1
description: Machine-readable account of what `ahwp edit --report <path>` (and `--dry-run`) did: every op's status, how many IR pieces it touched, and the segment ids it changed as before/after pairs. Since 1.1 a refused run writes this report too, with a top-level `refusal` and, when one op refused, the same `refusal` on that op (#531). Content-free outside `refusal` — no paragraph text, no replacement strings and no user-supplied patterns (T-07-22). A `refusal` names the structured inputs it refused on in `refusal.values`; `refusal.message` is a fixed, content-free sentence per code that never quotes request text, patterns, anchors, URLs, field or bookmark names or error chains (#348). The full human sentence goes to stderr only. Classify on `refusal.code`, never on the message.

schema_version.description: 1.1 (#531) adds the optional `refusal` objects and writes the report on refused runs; every 1.0 field is unchanged. 1.2 (#571) adds the `document_protected` refusal code; every 1.1 field and code is unchanged. 1.3 (#578) adds the `verify_mismatch` refusal code; every earlier field and code is unchanged. 1.4 (#583) adds the optional `preservation` list; every earlier field and code is unchanged. 1.5 (#577) adds the `raw_backed_edit` refusal code; every earlier field and code is unchanged. Writers emit 1.5.

dry_run.description: true when this report came from --dry-run: every op applied against an in-memory copy of the document through the same preflight, apply loop and staged writer/verifier a real run uses, but no output file was published (D-14). A dry-run report and a real-run report of the same batch differ only in this field.

preservation.description: 1.4 (#583). The typed preservation events of the run, in the shape of `hwp-preservation-report-v1` events: what the write removed or could not represent, with counts only and never document content. Absent when the run lost nothing. An `edit` from an HWP5 input to `.hwpx` runs the accounting `ahwp convert` runs for the same pair and publishes with the events that accounting adds, as `convert` does without `--strict`. Every event the HWPX writer itself reports still refuses that edit, as before (an opaque or image-filled control, an unrepresentable shape or header, a dropped binary, a dropped range tag), and of the added events `paragraph_range_tag_unrepresentable` and `font_type_info_unrepresentable` refuse too. `--verify` in that direction accepts a difference only when it is a named format projection or is covered by a reported event.

refusal.description: Present only when the run was refused and nothing was published (1.1). When an op refused, equal to that op's `refusal`; when the refusal was not tied to one op (loading, preflight, ops-file validation, writer or preservation checks), `ops` may be empty.

code.description: Stable snake_case id, named like the preservation-report-v1 event codes. `range_tag_shift`: An edit would move or drop an uninterpreted PARA_RANGE_TAG range mark. values: {}. `section_owner_insert`: An insertion would land in front of a section's setup paragraph. values: {}. `section_owner_move`: A move would land in front of a section's setup paragraph. values: {}. `add_table.anchor_not_found`: No top-level paragraph contains the add_table anchor. values: anchor (string, as given). `insert_blocks.unknown_style`: A style used by insert_blocks is not in the target and was not created (no definition, or missing_style=refuse). values: style (string), missing_style (create|refuse). `insert_blocks.invalid_definition`: A style definition could not be compiled, or the DocumentSpec issues sit under $.styles or $.lists. values: style and detail (string) for a compile failure; issues and container_width_mm for a validation failure. `insert_blocks.style_not_paragraph`: The named target style is not a paragraph style. values: style. `insert_blocks.duplicate_style`: The target holds the style name more than once. values: style. `insert_blocks.style_cycle`: based_on forms a cycle. values: style. `insert_blocks.style_id_overflow`: The style id does not fit HWP's one byte. values: style, style_id, max_style_id (integers). `layout_overflow`: DocumentSpec validation found a width that exceeds the insertion container. values: issues (list of {code, path, message, measured_width_mm?}, path a list of segments: strings, and integers for array indices; measured_width_mm is the image or table width, or the column sum, that overflowed, one decimal), container_width_mm (number, one decimal). `insert_blocks.invalid_spec`: DocumentSpec validation failed with no layout_overflow and no style or list issue. values: issues, container_width_mm, as for layout_overflow. `preservation_loss`: The writer would remove or change data it cannot preserve. values: events (list of {code, resource, disposition, count}; code is a preservation-report-v1 event code). `unapplied_requests`: Some requests matched nothing and --allow-partial was not given. values: {}; the failed entries of `ops` name which requests missed. `no_applicable_edits`: No request changed the document. values: {}. `document_protected` (1.2): The input document is protected and cannot be opened. values: protection (string), one of `password` (a password is required or the one given is wrong; the engine does not tell the two apart, HWP5 and HWPX), `certificate_encryption`, `certificate_drm`, `drm` or `signature` (the HWP5 FileHeader gates). A distribution document is not refused here, since it is readable. `verify_mismatch` (1.3): with --verify, the re-read output differs from the edited document. values: counts (list of {name, expected, actual}, the count invariants that differ; name is one of sections, paragraphs, tables, pictures, generic_controls, fields, bookmarks, hyperlinks, bin_streams, char_shapes, para_shapes, styles, text_chars, and the values are counts, never document content). An empty list means only the canonical digest differs. Since 1.4, missing_element (optional, one of footnote_shape, endnote_shape, page_border_fill) names the section element an HWP5 to HWPX edit lost; then counts may be empty. Nothing is published. `raw_backed_edit` (1.5): An edit changed the text of a control that the HWP5 writer writes from its saved records (a text box or other shape, a footnote, endnote, header or footer read from a saved file), so the edit would have been dropped while the run reported success. Raised for an HWP5 input written as `.hwp`, with or without --verify, and nothing is published. values: controls (list of {kind, count}: kind is one of footnote, endnote, header, footer, shape_or_text_box, other, count the controls whose text the edit changed). The same edit to a `.hwpx` output is written. `unclassified`: Any other refusal. values: {}. Its message is the fixed sentence for `unclassified`; the full sentence is on stderr only.

values.description: The structured inputs behind the refusal, per code (see `code`). User-typed strings (anchors, style names) appear here as given, never spliced into `code` or into a path segment.

message.description: A fixed, content-free sentence for `code` (Korean); it never interpolates request content (#348). The full human sentence is on stderr only. Its wording may change between releases.

index.description: This op's position in the --ops batch array (Phase 6 D-01 array order).

op.description: The op kind, spelled the same way edit-ops-v1's own "op" field spells it (Phase 6 D-03).

pieces_touched.description: For apply_form_bindings, the number of selected text replacements plus newly cloned profile tables (the original table is not a clone); the receipt separately reports targets and cloned_profiles, and changed remains empty. For insert_blocks, the number of inserted top-level paragraphs (one per accepted block, equal to blocks.len(); table cell paragraphs are inside their table and not counted). The ids of the inserted segments are in changed. For other operations, how many IR nodes this op actually mutated: the number of canonical runs whose shape id changed for a run-range char-format op, the number of segment ids (paragraph and/or run) an addressed op's own target touched otherwise, and never less than 1 for an applied op that changed the document — an "applied: 1" summary must never hide a multi-piece write (D-02). An applied op whose result was already in effect (a `style_tables` on already-styled tables, or a `set_table_placement` to the placement the table already has) changed nothing and reports 0 (#359).

changed.description: Before/after segment id pairs this op changed (D-13). insert_blocks reports one creation pair (before null) for every segment `ahwp cat --segments v2` publishes inside the inserted top-level paragraphs, in document order, in the state right after that op: each paragraph id followed by its run ids and, for a table or image block, the table, cell and image ids. An inserted top-level paragraph with no published segment (an empty or break-only one) is named by its paragraph id, which a fresh `ahwp cat --segments v2` does not list but move_para and delete_para accept (#521). A run id is what set_format addresses. pieces_touched counts the inserted paragraphs, not these pairs. Empty for an op with no address (a text-anchor/pattern match, which has no segment id to report) or one that changed nothing identifiable. A run-range char-format op that splits a run reports the touched paragraph's OWN id change AND the id change of every LATER run in that paragraph, not only the run it targeted — splitting a run shifts every later run's canonical index and therefore its id, even though that run's own text and shape are untouched; reporting only the targeted run's pair would leave a consumer re-keying against ids that no longer exist.

missing_style.description: Selected missing-style policy for applied insert_blocks only; omitted for every other outcome. The request defaults to create. This is policy metadata, not a failure reason.

changed_total.description: Present only when this op produced more id pairs than the 10000 that `changed` may carry: the real number of pairs. `changed` then holds the first 10000 in document order and the rest are not listed; they are still addressable, because every id is the one `ahwp cat --segments v2` publishes for the output. Absent means `changed` is complete. A valid insert_blocks request can exceed the cap (for example one 100 x 50 table publishes 15002 segments: the paragraph, the table, and a cell, a cell paragraph and a run for each of its 5000 cells), and this field keeps the report valid instead of dropping the edit's id list silently.

refusal.description: Present only on the failed op that refused the run (1.1).

reason.description: Populated only when status is "failed"; null when applied. A fixed, content-free label: usually `<op>: <cause>`, naming the op kind and the failure class (for example `replace: no match`, `create_field: anchor not found`), and a fixed notice for an op whose miss preflight already reported (an unresolved `set_cell_by_label` label). It never repeats the request's patterns, replacement strings, anchors, names or urls, nor any document text (#348). Its wording may change between releases; match on `op` and `status`, not on this text.

before.description: The segment id before this op applied. null marks a creation — the segment did not exist before the batch.

after.description: The segment id after this op applied. null marks a removal — the segment no longer exists after the batch.
